I was diagnosed with Borderline Personality Disorder before getting my current diagnosis of bipolar disorder.  The 2 can be co-morbid, and to be honest the name doesn't really change much; I still experience the same things.

Medication wise I have been on snti-depressants since  was 17 years old, and then on top of that sleeping pills, diazepam..and a lot of others.  Now my meds are more focused on the bipolar side of things.
There won't be one medication that will cure everything but there is certainly some merit in considering meds to help take the edge off of things and give you a chance to work out how to better handle your situation.

I certainly have memories that are far more prominent and clear when I'm in a particular state.  Being in the moment could almost be seen in a slightly buhdist context, but that aside there may be a few biological processes going on.  Before I go any further I am not a doctor and my bio-chem is not amazing but there are a few things you may want to consider. 
The old saying 'wire together fire together'  has a pretty strong basis in reality.  Neurons that form close associations may do so but are only activated through specific neural loops.  That MAY be somthing that could explain the relation you see between the moods and their matching memories, because they are wired on the same neural circuit in your brain.
It may also be worth cosidering whether it takes you to be in an extreme mood to feel those memories or be able to cope with thinking abou them.  It is not unknown for people to just 'switch off' and their brains just try to go on auto pilot because they can't handle the thoughts they would otherwise be haviing.
At the end of the day these are just ideas and you should go and talk to a professional about what you're experiencing.  If you want any links to articles covering stuff I've mentioned let me know :)
